Best Crypto Exchanges for Futures in Canada (2026)

Guides · 7 min read · Updated June 2026

Trading crypto from Canada in 2026 comes with a catch: the regulatory landscape shifted, and several of the big offshore names you'll see in global "best exchange" lists no longer serve Canadian residents. Here's the honest picture.

What changed

The Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) tightened expectations for crypto trading platforms serving residents — pushing them to register or file a pre-registration undertaking. Rather than comply, Binance exited Canada in 2023, and other offshore venues limited or paused Canadian activity. The upshot: don't assume a globally popular exchange accepts Canadians — verify it directly.

What to look for in a Canadian platform

Prioritise, in order: (1) registration or a pre-registration undertaking with Canadian regulators; (2) CAD deposits/withdrawals so you're not eating FX twice; (3) transparent, all-in fees; and (4) clear custody and proof-of-reserves. Kraken has long served Canadian customers and is a common regulated choice; always confirm current product availability (especially for derivatives) for your province before funding. Our checklist for vetting any venue is in how to evaluate a new exchange.

Leverage is capped lower — that's fine

Regulated Canadian offerings cap leverage well below the 100x offshore perps. That's protective, not limiting: the leverage those offshore venues advertise is exactly what liquidates most retail accounts. What actually preserves capital is sizing and stops, not max leverage.

Practice before you pick

Whatever platform you land on, learn the mechanics where there's no regulation and no risk: a free paper trading account on live prices. Find your liquidation price, size positions properly, and rehearse volatile calendar events — then move to a registered Canadian exchange with the skill already built.
